statement: The rational triple in Theorem 4.3 is strongly general and has 184 distinct geometric tangent circles: 160 real circles with positive squared radius and 24 nonreal circles forming 12 conjugate pairs. The same real count persists on a nonempty Euclidean open set. Fourfold splitting plus exact Sturm–Tarski and rational interval/elimination certificates establish 160<=M_R<=184; maximality of 160 remains unproved.

source.location: Theorems 1.1, 4.2 and 4.3; Section 6.1, fixed rational fibre delta_0=1/500000 (attainability consequence)

scope: Three general complex plane conics; circles are conics through the two circular points at infinity.
notes: An individual attainable count; this does not settle the complete spectrum.
